01 / WHY IT MATTERS

Parallel data, one wire at a time.

Most buses inside a chip are parallel, but many links between chips — SPI, sensor lines, long cables — only have one data wire. A shift register is the bridge: it converts a wide parallel word into a slow serial stream, or the reverse, one clock edge at a time.

01
LOAD OR FEED
Parallel bits loaded, or serial bits fed in one at a time
02
SHIFT EACH CLOCK
Every edge, bits move one position toward the output end
03
READ THE RESULT
Serial or parallel output is valid once shifting completes
💡 WHAT IS HAPPENING?

One clock. One bit moves.

On every rising edge, the register samples its input, shifts its stored bits right by one position, and emits whatever fell off the end. After N edges, all N bits originally fed in have either passed through or settled into place.

03 / INTERNAL LOGIC

Shift-right register logic

Each clock edge: capture the input bit at the MSB end, shift every other bit one place to the right, and emit the old LSB as serial output.

on clock_edge:
  so = state[width-1]
  state = [serial_in] + state[0 : width-1]

07 / PROJECT NOTES

Documentation

The implementation follows a digital-logic-first approach: define the shift model before adding the visualization layer.

Project objective
Visualize how SISO / SIPO / PISO / PIPO shift registers convert between serial and parallel data, one clock at a time.
Assumptions
Registers power up cleared to 0, shift right (MSB in, LSB out), inputs are strictly binary, and PISO/PIPO loads must match the register width exactly.
Future improvements
Add left-shift mode, multi-register cascading, and a bit-error-rate view for noisy serial links.
READMELAB NOTELOCAL MODEL

Right-shift register model

On every clock edge the register captures the serial input at the MSB, shifts every bit one place toward the LSB, and emits the bit that falls off the end as serial output. Parallel modes load or read the whole word in one step instead of shifting.

if mode in (SISO, SIPO):
  so = shift_step(serial_in)
if mode == PISO:
  load(parallel_in); then shift N times, SI=0
